summary: Independent review of Release Intelligence v2.0.0-GA GOLDEN BUILD ZIP SHA256 96ff7a49e2707682511017abbda6dabda6ef1e8370649061a63300415020b5fc. All 27 packaged files byte-match source. Method validation now uses the same measure, team, epic titles, and summaries supplied to the model, with explicit goal-versus-outcome instructions. The method-only system override retains read-only and untrusted-evidence constraints. Successful groups remain available when another group fails; failed groups display and copy clearly labeled original source summaries rather than fabricated AI consolidation. Dynamic output remains escaped and no backend write path is introduced. Branding and version identifiers match the requested GA designation. Independently executed all 15 focused AI tests successfully. No blocking issues found. Overall application risk remains High under the existing rubric assessment.
caveats: GA/GOLDEN BUILD is the requested release designation, not evidence that inherited operational risks or production-model behavior have been eliminated.

Numbers in epic titles or measures can describe targets or identifiers rather than achieved outcomes. Validation checks numeric presence, not semantic correctness; human review must distinguish goals, accomplishments, chronology, and coverage.
Mixed results intentionally retain successful AI groups and explicitly labeled source-only groups. Copied source-only sections remain source summaries, not a completed method consolidation.
Production SDK handling of systemPromptOverride and actual hosted model output were not verified because the hosted browser connector remained unavailable.
Automatic correction can add one SDK request per group within the shared timeout. Method results use the generated epic-summary snapshot, and upstream work may continue after cancellation.
Current GUS Apps host metadata still relies on verified-definition snapshots; future automatic list-column detection remains unavailable without live list-view REST capability.

Existing temporal-evidence, preview caching, popup accessibility/scroll, refresh concurrency, journal growth, revision conflicts, non-atomic updates, preference semantics, host/catalog/history limits, and AllUsers sharing caveats remain.

This review combined static source/artifact inspection with 15 independently executed focused AI tests. The implementing agent reported all 135 Node tests and method, monthly-AI, and Escape browser suites passed; those full suites and production-host/model behavior were not independently verified. Git and Pages publication were outside this review.
